sanskrit: tasmin mahābhaye ghore tumule lomaharṣaṇe vavarṣuḥ śaravarṣāṇi kṣatriyā yuddhadurmadāḥ
english: In that dread and fearful tumult, that hair-raising turmoil, the warriors, drunk with the frenzy of battle, poured down their showers of arrows.

sanskrit: krośanti kuñjarās tatra śaravarṣapratāpitāḥ tāvakānāṃ pareṣāṃ ca saṃyuge bharatottama aśvāś ca paryadhāvanta hatārohā diśo daśa
english: There the elephants, scorched by the rain of arrows, trumpeted in agony—both yours and the enemy's, O best of the Bharatas, in that clash—and the horses, their riders slain, fled wildly across the ten directions.

sanskrit: utpatya nipatanty anye śaraghātaprapīḍitāḥ tāvakānāṃ pareṣāṃ ca yodhānāṃ bharatarṣabha
english: Others, tormented by the blows of arrows, leaped up and fell again—warriors of yours and of the foe alike, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: aśvānāṃ kuñjarāṇāṃ ca rathānāṃ cātivartatām saṃghātāḥ sma pradṛśyante tatra tatra viśāṃ pate
english: Heaped-up masses of horses, of elephants, and of careering chariots could be seen here and there, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: gadābhir asibhiḥ prāsair bāṇaiś ca nataparvabhiḥ jaghnuḥ parasparaṃ tatra kṣatriyāḥ kālacoditāḥ
english: With maces and swords, with javelins and with smooth-jointed shafts, the warriors, driven on by Death, struck one another there.

sanskrit: apare bāhubhir vīrā niyuddhakuśalā yudhi bahudhā samasajjanta āyasaiḥ parighair iva
english: Other heroes, skilled in unarmed combat, grappled in the fray with their bare arms in many a way, as though with bars of iron.

sanskrit: muṣṭibhir jānubhiś caiva talaiś caiva viśāṃ pate anyonyaṃ jaghnire vīrās tāvakāḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha
english: With fists and knees and open palms, O lord of peoples, the heroes smote each other—your men together with the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: virathā rathinaś cātra nistriṃśavaradhāriṇaḥ anyonyam abhidhāvanta parasparavadhaiṣiṇaḥ
english: And there chariot-warriors stripped of their cars, wielding their excellent swords, rushed upon one another, each bent on the other's slaughter.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā kaliṅgair bahubhir vṛtaḥ puraskṛtya raṇe bhīṣmaṃ pāṇḍavān abhyavartata
english: Then King Duryodhana, surrounded by a host of Kaliṅgas, placing Bhīṣma at the head of the battle, advanced against the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavāḥ sarve parivārya vṛkodaram bhīṣmam abhyadravan kruddhā raṇe rabhasavāhanāḥ
english: And so too all the Pāṇḍavas, ranging themselves about Vṛkodara, charged in fury upon Bhīṣma in battle, their steeds borne on with headlong speed.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca dṛṣṭvā bhīṣmeṇa saṃsaktān bhrātṝn anyāṃś ca pārthivān tam abhyadhāvad gāṅgeyam udyatāstro dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing his brothers and the other princes locked in combat with Bhīṣma, Dhanaṃjaya, his weapon upraised, rushed upon the son of Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: pāñcajanyasya nirghoṣaṃ dhanuṣo gāṇḍivasya ca dhvajaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā pārthasya sarvān no bhayam āviśat
english: At the blare of the Pāñcajanya and of the Gāṇḍīva bow, and at the sight of Pārtha's banner, terror entered into us all.

sanskrit: asajjamānaṃ vṛkṣeṣu dhūmaketum ivotthitam bahuvarṇaṃ ca citraṃ ca divyaṃ vānaralakṣaṇam apaśyāma mahārāja dhvajaṃ gāṇḍivadhanvanaḥ
english: Catching upon no tree, risen like a blazing comet, many-hued and wondrous, divine and bearing the mark of the ape—such, O great king, did we behold the banner of the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: vidyutaṃ meghamadhyasthāṃ bhrājamānām ivāmbare dadṛśur gāṇḍivaṃ yodhā rukmapṛṣṭhaṃ mahārathe
english: Like lightning set amid the clouds, gleaming in the sky, the warriors beheld the gold-backed Gāṇḍīva in the hands of that mighty car-warrior.

sanskrit: aśuśruma bhṛśaṃ cāsya śakrasyevābhigarjataḥ sughoraṃ talayoḥ śabdaṃ nighnatas tava vāhinīm
english: And we heard, loud as the thunder of Śakra, the dread clap of his palms as he smote down your host.

sanskrit: caṇḍavāto yathā meghaḥ savidyutstanayitnumān diśaḥ saṃplāvayan sarvāḥ śaravarṣaiḥ samantataḥ
english: As a storm-cloud driven by a fierce wind, charged with lightning and thunder, floods all the quarters with rain, so on every side he deluged them with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: abhyadhāvata gāṅgeyaṃ bhairavāstro dhanaṃjayaḥ diśaṃ prācīṃ pratīcīṃ ca na jānīmo 'stramohitāḥ
english: Dhanaṃjaya, wielding his terrible weapons, rushed upon the son of Gaṅgā; bewildered by his missiles, we no longer knew the east from the west.

sanskrit: kāṃdigbhūtāḥ śrāntapatrā hatāstrā hatacetasaḥ anyonyam abhisaṃśliṣya yodhās te bharatarṣabha
english: Lost as to which way to turn, their plumes drooping, their weapons spent and their wits undone, those warriors clung one to another, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: bhīṣmam evābhilīyanta saha sarvais tavātmajaiḥ teṣām ārtāyanam abhūd bhīṣmaḥ śaṃtanavo raṇe
english: They sought refuge with Bhīṣma alone, together with all your sons; in that battle Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, became the haven of the afflicted.

sanskrit: samutpatanta vitrastā rathebhyo rathinas tadā sādinaś cāśvapṛṣṭhebhyo bhūmau cāpi padātayaḥ
english: Then the car-warriors in terror leaped from their chariots, the horsemen from the backs of their steeds, and the foot-soldiers sank to the ground.

sanskrit: śrutvā gāṇḍīvanirghoṣaṃ visphūrjitam ivāśaneḥ sarvasainyāni bhītāni vyavalīyanta bhārata
english: Hearing the roar of the Gāṇḍīva, like the crash of a thunderbolt, all the armies in their fear melted away, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: atha kāmbojamukhyais tu bṛhadbhiḥ śīghragāmibhiḥ gopānāṃ bahusāhasrair balair govāsano vṛtaḥ
english: Then the lord of the cowherds, Govāsana, came surrounded by the foremost Kāmbojas—tall and swift of foot—and by the many thousands of herdsmen's forces.

sanskrit: madrasauvīragāndhārais trigartaiś ca viśāṃ pate sarvakāliṅgamukhyaiś ca kaliṅgādhipatir vṛtaḥ
english: And the lord of the Kaliṅgas was ringed about by the Madras, Sauvīras, and Gāndhāras, by the Trigartas, O lord of peoples, and by all the chief warriors of the Kaliṅgas.

sanskrit: nāgā naragaṇaughāś ca duḥśāsanapuraḥsarāḥ jayadrathaś ca nṛpatiḥ sahitaḥ sarvarājabhiḥ
english: Elephants and great hosts of men, with Duḥśāsana at their head, and King Jayadratha together with all the kings—

sanskrit: hayārohavarāś caiva tava putreṇa coditāḥ caturdaśa sahasrāṇi saubalaṃ paryavārayan
english: and excellent horsemen, fourteen thousand strong, urged on by your son, encircled the son of Subala.

sanskrit: tatas te sahitāḥ sarve vibhaktarathavāhanāḥ pāṇḍavān samare jagmus tāvakā bharatarṣabha
english: Then all your men together, with their chariots and mounts marshalled apart, advanced upon the Pāṇḍavas in battle, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: rathibhir vāraṇair aśvaiḥ padātaiś ca samīritam ghoram āyodhanaṃ jajñe mahābhrasadṛśaṃ rajaḥ
english: Stirred up by car-warriors, elephants, horses, and foot-soldiers, the dread dust of battle arose, resembling a great mass of clouds.

sanskrit: tomaraprāsanārācagajāśvarathayodhinām balena mahatā bhīṣmaḥ samasajjat kirīṭinā
english: With a mighty host of warriors fighting with lances, javelins, and iron shafts, mounted on elephants, horses, and chariots, Bhīṣma closed with the Diademed one.

sanskrit: āvantyaḥ kāśirājena bhīmasenena saindhavaḥ ajātaśatrur madrāṇām ṛṣabheṇa yaśasvinā sahaputraḥ sahāmātyaḥ śalyena samasajjata
english: The lord of Avanti closed with the king of Kāśi, the lord of Sindhu with Bhīmasena; and Ajātaśatru, with his sons and counsellors, engaged the glorious bull of the Madras, Śalya.

sanskrit: vikarṇaḥ sahadevena citrasenaḥ śikhaṇḍinā matsyā duryodhanaṃ jagmuḥ śakuniṃ ca viśāṃ pate
english: Vikarṇa engaged Sahadeva, Citrasena engaged Śikhaṇḍin, and the Matsyas advanced against Duryodhana and against Śakuni, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: drupadaś cekitānaś ca sātyakiś ca mahārathaḥ droṇena samasajjanta saputreṇa mahātmanā kṛpaś ca kṛtavarmā ca dhṛṣṭaketum abhidrutau
english: Drupada, Cekitāna, and the great car-warrior Sātyaki closed with the high-souled Droṇa and his son; while Kṛpa and Kṛtavarman rushed together upon Dhṛṣṭaketu.

sanskrit: evaṃ prajavitāśvāni bhrāntanāgarathāni ca sainyāni samasajjanta prayuddhāni samantataḥ
english: Thus the armies, their horses galloping and their elephants and chariots wheeling about, closed and grappled in furious combat on every side.

sanskrit: nirabhre vidyutas tīvrā diśaś ca rajasāvṛtāḥ prādurāsan maholkāś ca sanirghātā viśāṃ pate
english: Though the sky was cloudless, fierce lightnings flashed and the quarters were veiled in dust; great meteors appeared, attended by crashing thunderclaps, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: pravavau ca mahāvātaḥ pāṃsuvarṣaṃ papāta ca nabhasy antardadhe sūryaḥ sainyena rajasāvṛtaḥ
english: A great wind blew, a rain of dust came down, and in the heavens the sun was hidden away, mantled by the dust raised by the host.

sanskrit: pramohaḥ sarvasattvānām atīva samapadyata rajasā cābhibhūtānām astrajālaiś ca tudyatām
english: An utter bewilderment came upon all living things, overwhelmed as they were by the dust and tormented by the nets of weapons.

sanskrit: vīrabāhuvisṛṣṭānāṃ sarvāvaraṇabhedinām saṃghātaḥ śarajālānāṃ tumulaḥ samapadyata
english: A tumultuous massing of webs of arrows arose—shafts loosed from the arms of heroes, piercing through every kind of armour.

sanskrit: prakāśaṃ cakrur ākāśam udyatāni bhujottamaiḥ nakṣatravimalābhāni śastrāṇi bharatarṣabha
english: Weapons upraised by mighty arms, bright as the stars, lit up the firmament, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: ārṣabhāṇi vicitrāṇi rukmajālāvṛtāni ca saṃpetur dikṣu sarvāsu carmāṇi bharatarṣabha
english: Shields of bull's hide, of varied hue and overlaid with networks of gold, flew through all the quarters, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: sūryavarṇaiś ca nistriṃśaiḥ pātyamānāni sarvaśaḥ dikṣu sarvāsv adṛśyanta śarīrāṇi śirāṃsi ca
english: Struck down on every side by swords bright as the sun, bodies and heads were seen falling throughout all the quarters.

sanskrit: bhagnacakrākṣanīḍāś ca nipātitamahādhvajāḥ hatāśvāḥ pṛthivīṃ jagmus tatra tatra mahārathāḥ
english: With wheels, axles, and chariot-boxes shattered, their tall banners cast down and their horses slain, the great car-warriors sank to the earth here and there.

sanskrit: paripetur hayāś cātra ke cic chastrakṛtavraṇāḥ rathān viparikarṣanto hateṣu rathayodhiṣu
english: And here some horses, wounded by weapons, ran wildly about, dragging the chariots after them, their car-warriors slain.

sanskrit: śarāhatā bhinnadehā baddhayoktrā hayottamāḥ yugāni paryakarṣanta tatra tatra sma bhārata
english: Struck by arrows, their bodies torn, yet still bound in their harness, the finest of steeds dragged the yokes about here and there, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: adṛśyanta sasūtāś ca sāśvāḥ sarathayodhinaḥ ekena balinā rājan vāraṇena hatā rathāḥ
english: Chariots could be seen, with their drivers, their horses, and their fighting men, all slain together by a single mighty elephant, O king.

sanskrit: gandhahastimadasrāvam āghrāya bahavo raṇe saṃnipāte balaughānāṃ vītam ādadire gajāḥ
english: Catching in the battle the scent of the rut flowing from the lordly tuskers, many an elephant, at the clash of those floods of troops, took to flight.

sanskrit: satomaramahāmātrair nipatadbhir gatāsubhiḥ babhūvāyodhanaṃ channaṃ nārācābhihatair gajaiḥ
english: The field of battle was covered over with elephants struck down by iron shafts, falling lifeless together with their lances and their mighty riders.

sanskrit: saṃnipāte balaughānāṃ preṣitair varavāraṇaiḥ nipetur yudhi saṃbhagnāḥ sayodhāḥ sadhvajā rathāḥ
english: At the clash of those floods of troops, chariots—shattered by the lordly elephants hurled against them—fell in battle together with their warriors and their banners.

sanskrit: nāgarājopamair hastair nāgair ākṣipya saṃyuge vyadṛśyanta mahārāja saṃbhagnā rathakūbarāḥ
english: Seized in battle by the trunks of elephants huge as the king of serpents, chariot-poles could be seen snapped asunder, O great king.

sanskrit: viśīrṇarathajālāś ca keśeṣv ākṣipya dantibhiḥ drumaśākhā ivāvidhya niṣpiṣṭā rathino raṇe
english: Their lattice-work of chariots smashed, the car-warriors were seized by the hair by the tuskers, whirled about like the branches of trees, and ground to pieces in the fray.

sanskrit: ratheṣu ca rathān yuddhe saṃsaktān varavāraṇāḥ vikarṣanto diśaḥ sarvāḥ saṃpetuḥ sarvaśabdagāḥ
english: Dragging chariot upon chariot, locked together in the fight, the lordly elephants rushed in every direction, plunging through every clamour.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tathā karṣatāṃ ca gajānāṃ rūpam ābabhau saraḥsu nalinījālaṃ viṣaktam iva karṣatām
english: As they dragged their burdens so, those elephants had the look of beasts hauling a tangle of lotus-stalks caught fast in the pools.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃchāditaṃ tatra babhūvāyodhanaṃ mahat sādibhiś ca padātaiś ca sadhvajaiś ca mahārathaiḥ
english: Thus was that vast field of battle covered over with horsemen and foot-soldiers and with great car-warriors and their banners.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śikhaṇḍī saha matsyena virāṭena viśāṃ pate bhīṣmam āśu maheṣvāsam āsasāda sudurjayam
english: Saṃjaya said: Śikhaṇḍin, together with Virāṭa of the Matsyas, O lord of peoples, swiftly fell upon Bhīṣma, that great archer most hard to conquer.

sanskrit: droṇaṃ kṛpaṃ vikarṇaṃ ca maheṣvāsān mahābalān rājñaś cānyān raṇe śūrān bahūn ārchad dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Dhanaṃjaya assailed Droṇa, Kṛpa, and Vikarṇa—great archers of mighty strength—and many other heroic kings in the battle.

sanskrit: saindhavaṃ ca maheṣvāsaṃ sāmātyaṃ saha bandhubhiḥ prācyāṃś ca dākṣiṇātyāṃś ca bhūmipān bhūmiparṣabha
english: And the lord of Sindhu, that great archer, with his counsellors and kinsmen, and the kings of the East and of the South, O bull among lords of the earth—

sanskrit: putraṃ ca te maheṣvāsaṃ duryodhanam amarṣaṇam duḥsahaṃ caiva samare bhīmaseno 'bhyavartata
english: and against your son, the great archer, the unforgiving Duryodhana, and against Duḥsaha as well, did Bhīmasena advance in battle.

sanskrit: sahadevas tu śakunim ulūkaṃ ca mahāratham pitāputrau maheṣvāsāv abhyavartata durjayau
english: But Sahadeva advanced upon Śakuni and the great car-warrior Ulūka—father and son, both great archers hard to vanquish.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiro mahārāja gajānīkaṃ mahārathaḥ samavartata saṃgrāme putreṇa nikṛtas tava
english: Yudhiṣṭhira, O great king, that mighty car-warrior, met in battle the host of elephants—he whom your son had so wronged.

sanskrit: mādrīputras tu nakulaḥ śūraḥ saṃkrandano yudhi trigartānāṃ rathodāraiḥ samasajjata pāṇḍavaḥ
english: And the son of Mādrī, the valiant Nakula, raising his war-cry in the fray, that Pāṇḍava engaged the noble chariot-warriors of the Trigartas.

sanskrit: abhyavartanta durdharṣāḥ samare śālvakekayān sātyakiś cekitānaś ca saubhadraś ca mahārathaḥ
english: The unassailable Sātyaki, Cekitāna, and the great car-warrior, son of Subhadrā, advanced in battle against the Śālvas and Kekayas.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭaketuś ca samare rākṣasaś ca ghaṭotkacaḥ putrāṇāṃ te rathānīkaṃ pratyudyātāḥ sudurjayāḥ
english: And Dhṛṣṭaketu and the rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca, hard indeed to overcome, advanced in battle against the chariot-host of your sons.

sanskrit: senāpatir ameyātmā dhṛṣṭadyumno mahābalaḥ droṇena samare rājan samiyāyendrakarmaṇā
english: The commander of the army, the immeasurable-souled and mighty Dhṛṣṭadyumna, closed in battle, O king, with Droṇa, whose deeds were like Indra's.

sanskrit: evam ete maheṣvāsās tāvakāḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha sametya samare śūrāḥ saṃprahāraṃ pracakrire
english: Thus did these great archers, your heroes, meeting the Pāṇḍavas in battle, set to and join the fight.

sanskrit: madhyaṃdinagate sūrye nabhasy ākulatāṃ gate kuravaḥ pāṇḍaveyāś ca nijaghnur itaretaram
english: When the sun had reached the midst of the sky and the heavens had fallen into turmoil, the Kurus and the sons of Pāṇḍu slew one another.

sanskrit: dhvajino hemacitrāṅgā vicaranto raṇājire sapatākā rathā rejur vaiyāghraparivāraṇāḥ
english: Bearing their standards, their frames bright with gold, ranging over the field of battle, the chariots with their pennons and their coverings of tiger-skin shone resplendent.

sanskrit: sametānāṃ ca samare jigīṣūṇāṃ parasparam babhūva tumulaḥ śabdaḥ siṃhānām iva nardatām
english: From those who had met in battle, each longing to overcome the other, there arose a tumultuous din, like that of roaring lions.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma saṃprahāraṃ sudāruṇam yam akurvan raṇe vīrāḥ sṛñjayāḥ kurubhiḥ saha
english: There we beheld a wondrous and most terrible encounter, which the heroic Sṛñjayas waged in battle against the Kurus.

sanskrit: naiva khaṃ na diśo rājan na sūryaṃ śatrutāpana vidiśo vāpy apaśyāma śarair muktaiḥ samantataḥ
english: Neither the sky nor the quarters, O king, nor the sun, O scorcher of foes, nor even the intermediate points could we see, for the arrows loosed on every side.

sanskrit: śaktīnāṃ vimalāgrāṇāṃ tomarāṇāṃ tathāsyatām nistriṃśānāṃ ca pītānāṃ nīlotpalanibhāḥ prabhāḥ
english: From the spears with their gleaming points, from the lances hurled, and from the burnished swords, came radiances like the hue of blue lotuses.

sanskrit: kavacānāṃ vicitrāṇāṃ bhūṣaṇānāṃ prabhās tathā khaṃ diśaḥ pradiśaś caiva bhāsayām āsur ojasā virarāja tadā rājaṃs tatra tatra raṇāṅgaṇam
english: The splendours of the many-coloured cuirasses and of the ornaments lit up with their brilliance the sky, the quarters, and the intermediate quarters; and there, O king, the field of battle shone resplendent in every part.

sanskrit: rathasiṃhāsanavyāghrāḥ samāyāntaś ca saṃyuge virejuḥ samare rājan grahā iva nabhastale
english: Tigers among men upon their lion-thrones of chariots, advancing into the fray, shone forth in battle, O king, like the planets in the vault of heaven.

sanskrit: bhīṣmas tu rathināṃ śreṣṭho bhīmasenaṃ mahābalam avārayata saṃkruddhaḥ sarvasainyasya paśyataḥ
english: But Bhīṣma, the best of car-warriors, in his wrath held back the mighty Bhīmasena before the eyes of the whole army.

sanskrit: tato bhīṣmavinirmuktā rukmapuṅkhāḥ śilāśitāḥ abhyaghnan samare bhīmaṃ tailadhautāḥ sutejanāḥ
english: Then shafts loosed by Bhīṣma, gold-feathered and whetted on stone, polished with oil and keen-edged, smote Bhīma in the battle.

sanskrit: tasya śaktiṃ mahāvegāṃ bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ kruddhāśīviṣasaṃkāśāṃ preṣayām āsa bhārata
english: Against him the mighty Bhīmasena hurled a swift-flying spear, like an enraged venomous serpent, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā rukmadaṇḍāṃ durāsadām ciccheda samare bhīṣmaḥ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: As it came rushing on, that gold-shafted and irresistible spear, Bhīṣma cut asunder in the battle with his smooth-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: tato 'pareṇa bhallena pītena niśitena ca kārmukaṃ bhīmasenasya dvidhā ciccheda bhārata
english: Then with another broad-headed arrow, burnished and keen, he cut the bow of Bhīmasena in two, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sātyakis tu tatas tūrṇaṃ bhīṣmam āsādya saṃyuge śarair bahubhir ānarchat pitaraṃ te janeśvara
english: But Sātyaki then swiftly closed with Bhīṣma in the fray and assailed your sire with a multitude of arrows, O lord of men.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃdhāya vai tīkṣṇaṃ śaraṃ paramadāruṇam vārṣṇeyasya rathād bhīṣmaḥ pātayām āsa sārathim
english: Then, fitting to his bow a sharp and most dreadful arrow, Bhīṣma struck down the charioteer of the Vṛṣṇi hero from his car.

sanskrit: tasyāśvāḥ pradrutā rājan nihate rathasārathau tena tenaiva dhāvanti manomārutaraṃhasaḥ
english: His charioteer slain, his horses bolted, O king, and ran this way and that with the speed of thought and of the wind.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvasya sainyasya nisvanas tumulo 'bhavat hāhākāraś ca saṃjajñe pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām
english: Then from the whole army arose a tumultuous uproar, and a cry of dismay broke forth among the high-souled Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: abhidravata gṛhṇīta hayān yacchata dhāvata ity āsīt tumulaḥ śabdo yuyudhānarathaṃ prati
english: "Rush in! Seize them! Hold the horses! Run!"—such was the tumultuous clamour that arose about the chariot of Yuyudhāna.
